build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player assigns crew members to station modules by dragging portraits, with each module requiring staffing to function and crew having skill ratings that affect performance. Score 0 if no crew assignment exists.
A power distribution system limits how many modules can be active simultaneously, and the player allocates power through a visible interface. Score 0 if no power system exists.

Random events fire periodically (supply ships, distress signals, system malfunctions, pirate attacks) requiring the player to respond via choice dialogs with visible consequences. Score 0 if no event system exists.
Crew fatigue accumulates with work and recovers with rest; overworked crew make mistakes that cause system failures. Score 0 if no fatigue system exists.
Life support must be maintained or crew health degrades; game over occurs if life support fails completely or all crew are incapacitated. Score 0 if no failure condition exists.
At least 6 distinct station modules (bridge, life support, power core, crew quarters, cargo bay, weapons, shields) with different functions and staffing needs. Score 0 if only one module exists.
At least 8 distinct random event types with different requirements and consequences (trade offers, combat, repairs, rescues, discoveries). Score 0 if only one event type exists.
New modules can be built using accumulated resources, expanding the station with at least 3 buildable additions beyond the starting layout. Score 0 if no building system exists.
Event severity escalates over 30+ cycles, with early events being manageable and later events requiring full station optimization to survive. Score 0 if difficulty never increases.
A cycle or game-end summary shows cycles survived, events handled, crew status, modules built, and resources remaining. Score 0 if the game ends abruptly with no summary.
Normal startup shows a styled title screen with the game name, space station silhouette, and starfield imagery. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The flow connects title to station overview to crew management to event responses to cycle summaries without restarting the executable. Score 0 if major transitions are missing.
The station overview clearly shows module status, power allocation, crew assignments, and resource levels in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot determine station state.

Player actions produce visible feedback: crew assignment shows them moving to modules, power changes update module indicators, events show alert animations, and damage shows module degradation. Score 0 if actions happen silently.

Art direction is coherent across title, station cross-section, modules, crew, events, and menus with a consistent sci-fi station palette and style. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.
Station modules, crew portraits, event illustrations, resources, and equipment use real sprite art with distinct sci-fi designs. Score 0 if primary elements are unstyled rectangles.
Animation brings the station to life: crew moving between modules, power fluctuation effects, event alert animations, module damage sparks, and starfield parallax. Score 0 if all elements are static.
HUD and UI panels use styled themed widgets with sci-fi console aesthetics, holographic frames, or space-station styling rather than raw HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all UI is default Label/Button.
